sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that as per the prosecution, about 7-8 months prior to the lodging of the FIR, when the victim was returning home from school, she was wrongfully restrained by the accused persons.
Accused Vikram S/o Karta Ram caught her from behind whereupon the petitioner Vikram S/o Bhoma Ram captured her photographs.
The petitioners by threatening the victim to make her photographs viral, subjected her to forcible sexual assault/rape on multiple occasions.

Learned counsel submitted that the petitioners, aged about 20 years and 18 years, are in judicial custody; the statements of the victim have already been recorded before the competent criminal Court and therefore, now there is no apprehension of petitioners influencing her or tampering with the evidence and the trial of the case will take sufficiently long time, therefore, the benefit of bail may be granted to the accused-petitioners.
Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor and learned counsel for the complainant have vehemently opposed the bail applications.
However, learned Public Prosecutor has not shown any apprehension of petitioners influencing remaining material prosecution witnesses of the case.

Having considered the rival submissions, facts and circumstances of the case, this Court prima facie finds that though the allegations levelled against the petitioners are very serious in nature but in view of the fact that the petitioners are aged about 20 and 18 years only and the statements of the victim have already been recorded before the competent criminal Court, therefore now (Uploaded on 07/11/2025 at 03:52:18 PM) [2025:RJ-JD:47783] (3 of 3) [CRLMB-1867/2025] there is no apprehension of petitioners influencing her or fleeing away from justice, the petitioners deserve a chance to face trial while on bail.
Thus, without expressing any opinion on merits/demerits of the case, this Court is of the opinion that the bail applications filed by the petitioners deserve to be accepted.
Consequently, these bail applications under Section 483 BNSS are allowed.

It is ordered that the accused-petitioners (1) Vikram Kumar S/o Karta Ram and (2) Vikram Kumar S/o Bhoma Ram arrested in connection with F.I.R. No.285/2024 registered at Police Station Bhinmal, District Jalore, shall be released on bail, if not wanted in any other case, provided each of them furnishes a personal bond of Rs.50,000/- and two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each, to the satisfaction of learned trial court, for their appearance before that court on each & every date of hearing and whenever called upon to do so till completion of the trial.
It is however, made clear that findings recorded/observations made above are for limited purposes of adjudication of bail application.
The trial court shall not get prejudiced by the same.
A copy of this order be placed in each file.

(KULDEEP MATHUR),J 183-184 divya/-
